title: FetchMan: Learning Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Policies from Simulated Experiences
method: Original PDF page rendered with Poppler at 200 dpi, cropped only; no redrawing or generated images.

figures.original_caption_text: Figure 1: F ETCH M AN learns visual humanoid loco-manipulation entirely in simulation and deploys it zero-shot to a real Unitree G1. The resulting policy walks up to and grasps objects across diverse, unseen real-world scenes, with no real-world data or per-scene tuning.

figures.original_caption_text: Figure 3: Synthetic data generation pipeline. Each episode samples (1) a house from MolmoSpaces, (2) a pickable target object within it, (3) a contact-free start and grasp-standoff goal pose connected by a planned path the scripted controller follows, and (4) domain randomization applied independently per episode.

figures.original_caption_text: Figure 4: Policy architecture. The head and wrist RGB streams are encoded by a frozen DINOv3 backbone into per-patch image tokens, while the proprioceptive vector (h t , r t , p t , q t upper , g t ) is mapped by an MLP to a single state token. A flow-matching DiT cross-attends to these tokens and denoises a 15-dimensional action chunk, split into upper-body targets (waist, arm, and gripper) tracked by a joint-level PD controller and a base command (v x , v y , ω, h̄ t ) executed by the pre-trained lower-body locomotion controller.

figures.original_caption_text: Figure 5: Two-stage training pipeline. Stage 1 (Imitation Pretraining). The task sampler instantiates diverse simulated environments in which the scripted G1 staged policy generates demonstration trajectories, and the resulting frozen dataset trains the loco-manipulation policy π by behavior cloning. Stage 2 (Online GRPO Refinement). The same sampler resets groups of environments to identical tasks (group size × number of groups), π collects on-policy trajectories that differ only in sampled action noise, and a group-relative GRPO update refines π in place.
